_about: Derived from src/tapper.asm, not written by hand -- Tapper's names live
in its source rather than in a symbol file, so this is a second view of
one reading. **If the two disagree, the source is right.**
`why` is the prose comment above each label there -- separator rules
and xref lists are formatting and are dropped. **122 of the 576 labels
have one**; the rest are block markers their author did not annotate,
and an empty `why` says so rather than inventing one. The `equ` entries
carry none either, for the same reason.
Addresses are runtime addresses (.COM, 0x100 already added), taken from
the address each instruction line carries in its trailing comment --
not from assembling, because src/tapper.asm does not assemble with NASM
2.16.03: `loop short` is rejected in six places, `loop` being short
already. BUILD.md promises 2.x or 3.x, so that is worth fixing there.
Moved into retro-ports on 2026-08-02. Two things changed in the move.
comrec's labels are and a key in the wrong coordinate substitutes nowhere
and says nothing about it.
And the reconstruction is no longer stored. src/tapper.asm assembled to a
byte-identical copy of TAPPER.COM -- the same SHA-256 -- which makes it
the game in source form, and this repository does not carry the game.
build.ps1 regenerates it into recovered/ from a copy you own.
Routine keys are file offsets, because that is what comrec labels are.
Global keys are addresses, because that is how a .COM listing writes a
memory operand. Getting the two the same way round substituted one
global in a hundred and seventy-six, silently.

_note: 16 bracketed constants are displacements, not addresses:
each appears only with a base register, never on its own, and every
one is under 0x400 -- a field inside a record the base points at.

_not_named: 133 addresses the listing references have no name.
They are Tapper's own variables, and they are left unnamed rather than
guessed. This game arrived from a separate repository where nothing
counted them; the other five here have none.
